DATES, SOURCES & LIMITS

The documented timeline

Verified dates and the kind of evidence behind each one are listed here. Factory ownership changes, dated publications and auction datings do not establish a continuous production history or a sequence of chair manufacturers.

Dated records

  1. 1944

    Designed as a gift for Peter

    Hans J. Wegner designed and made a chair as a christening gift for Peter, the son of his friend and fellow designer Børge Mogensen. The chair could be assembled and taken apart without tools. The exact day and month of the gift have not been established.

    Confirmed design date · manufacturer’s account

    Carl Hansen & Søn · CH410
  2. 1940s

    FDB Møbler: an auction-dated example

    Bukowskis attributes a surviving Peter’s Chair set to FDB Møbler and dates it to the 1940s. This is the dating of an auction object, not a verified manufacturing period. FDB’s first and last production years for the chair remain unknown.

    Auction documentation · full production period unknown

    Bukowskis · lot 1144431
  3. 6 January 1947

    Tarm factory: purchase agreement

    The museum’s factory history dates the purchase agreement for Tarm Stole- og Møbelfabrik to this day. This concerns the factory’s ownership. It does not establish when Peter’s Chair production began.

    Factory history only · not a chair-production date

    Vardemuseerne · Tarm factory history, p. 163
  4. 27 April 1947

    Tarm factory: formal FDB takeover

    The same factory history records FDB’s formal takeover of Tarm Stole- og Møbelfabrik on this date. This must not be used as Peter’s Chair’s production start, and it does not support describing Tarm as FDB-owned in 1944.

    Factory ownership milestone · chair-production period unknown

    Vardemuseerne · Tarm factory history, p. 163
  5. 1989

    Johannes Hansen: publication evidence

    Living Architecture no. 8, carrying a 1989 copyright date, shows Peter’s chair and table on printed page 106 with the maker code JH. The legend on printed page 109 identifies JH as Johannes Hansens Møbelsnedkeri. This is a dated documentary reference, not a production start or end date. Bunkamura’s later exhibition checklist independently attributes an Oda Collection chair to Johannes Hansen; its 1944 date is the design year.

    Dated publication + collection record · production boundaries unknown

    Living Architecture 8 · printed p. 106Living Architecture 8 · printed p. 109Bunkamura · exhibition checklist, pp. 1 and 3

Manufacturer evidence without verified dates

  • Dates unknown

    Fredericia Stolefabrik

    Quittenbaum auction records attribute surviving examples to A/S Fredericia Stolefabrik. These records support a Fredericia-made edition, but do not establish when production began or ended.

    Auction documentation · full period unknown

    Quittenbaum · auction 163C, lot 465

Current manufacturer

  • Current · checked 2026

    Carl Hansen & Søn · CH410

    Carl Hansen & Søn offers Peter’s Chair today as CH410 in untreated beech. The chair is documented in the company’s 2018 catalogue. The exact year Carl Hansen & Søn began producing it has not been established here.

    Current manufacturer confirmed · start date unknown

    Carl Hansen & Søn · CH410Carl Hansen & Søn · 2018 catalogue, pp. 188–189

A note on dates

A design date, the date assigned to an auction object, a publication date and a factory ownership date are different kinds of evidence. None, on its own, establishes a manufacturer’s first or last production year. The order of these entries does not imply a transfer of production from one manufacturer to the next. Unknown boundaries are left open.

Sources checked 14 October 2026 (Japan Standard Time)

Reading the manufacturing evidence

Tarm: ownership changed in 1947

The museum’s factory history dates the purchase agreement to 6 January 1947 and formal FDB control to 27 April 1947. These dates concern ownership of the factory. They neither establish when Peter’s Chair production began nor support describing Tarm as FDB-owned in 1944.

Vardemuseerne · Tarm factory history, p. 163

The reported 1944 production start

Carl Hansen & Søn's 2018 catalogue reports production beginning in 1944. That statement does not identify or date a complete production period for FDB or Tarm.

Carl Hansen & Søn · 2018 catalogue, pp. 188–189

Fritz Hansen: attribution not verified

This research did not find reliable evidence that Fritz Hansen manufactured Peter’s Chair. No production period is assigned to that maker; this is a limit of the verified evidence, not a claim that such production never occurred.

About this independent model

Four pieces were newly constructed from numerical profiles using overall dimensions and two-dimensional reference images. Nominal dimensions are 420 × 300 × 470 mm, with a 250 mm seat height. No manufacturer CAD or existing mesh geometry was imported. The synthetic wood textures were created for this model.

This is an unofficial visual approximation. Thicknesses, curves, openings and joints are estimates. It is not a fabrication plan, a verified assembly guide or a structural or safety assessment.

The model and viewer are included in this HTML file. Viewing needs no network connection; source links open external websites when selected.

The embedded data and interaction logic have been checked in code. The page has not been visually tested in a browser.

Independent modelling does not establish official endorsement, rights clearance or permission to manufacture or commercially reproduce the chair.
